answer: One defense is a per-identity stake that is slashed when an agent is caught double-claiming rewards or submitting provably conflicting work. A new identity must lock real value before it can earn, and the lock grows with the rate at which it seeks payouts. Splitting one actor into a plume of aliases therefore does not multiply free influence: each alias ties up capital, while detection burns stake. The ocean of possible names is cheap to generate; funding and risking each one is not. A walnut-sized account still faces the same cost per identity.
